questions.q: Where do you start when sharing a report from Power BI Desktop?
options: Email the .pbix file's data model to each stakeholder
Publish it to a workspace in the Power BI service, then share from there
Turn on Publish to web so everyone can reach it
Convert it to a Python script first
questions.explain: Sharing happens in the service. Publishing sends the semantic model and reports to a workspace and gives you a link.

questions.q: You made edits to a published report in the Power BI service. What happens to your original Desktop file?
options: It is updated automatically
It is deleted
It is not changed; service edits are not saved back to the Desktop file
It becomes read-only
questions.explain: Per Microsoft's documentation, changes made in the service are not saved back to the original Desktop file.

questions.q: Which sharing method best suits a larger team that should get a polished, read-only experience?
options: A direct link to one person
Publishing an app from a workspace
Publish to web
Emailing screenshots only
questions.explain: Apps package reports and dashboards for broader read-only distribution, per the sharing overview.

questions.q: A colleague suggests hiding a sensitive column in the report so viewers cannot see it. What is the right reaction?
options: Fine; hiding a column reliably blocks access to it
Only pages need hiding, not columns
Hiding removes the column from the data model entirely
Hiding is not a security measure; use row-level or object-level security on the semantic model
questions.explain: Microsoft's guidance says sharing a report shares its semantic model, and hidden elements can still be reached. Use RLS or OLS.

questions.q: Why might saving a chart as a PNG with matplotlib be the better deliverable?
options: Because images are always more accurate than reports
Because Power BI cannot publish charts
Because it avoids needing a data model at all for every dataset
Because stakeholders without Power BI access can still view it in an email or slide
questions.explain: Not every stakeholder uses Power BI or holds a license. A static image travels anywhere.
